Acquisition choices helped: the intermediate 3 uM well and 1 uM replicate proved persistence of the phenotype versus a single-well artefact. Verdict: approve.

Approve Aurora kinase inhibitors at p=0.62. Massive phenotype replicated in 3 wells (1uM reps 1-2 and 3uM): frac_large_nucleus z=+59 to +72, nuclear area/DNA-integrated up with form-factor/solidity down (z -26 to -53), plus multilobed polyploid nuclei on microscopy, intact tubulin/actin and low frac_mitotic_like. ## Unblinding

Compound: **AZ841** (PubChem CID [12001839](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/12001839))

Identity check: from the BBBC021 structure (the name is not in PubChem)

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: the call was **Aurora kinase inhibitors**, BBBC021 annotates **Aurora kinase inhibitors**.

## Reflection

The correct Aurora call rested on the replicated massive large-nucleus phenotype: frac_large_nucleus z=+60.3 at 1 uM rep1 (e2), +59.0 at 3 uM (e7) and +71.6 at 1 uM rep2 (e8) with very low form-factor/solidity and high nuclear area, plus the microscopist description of multilobed polyploid nuclei with intact cytoskeleton favoring Aurora (e5). I correctly down-weighted the protocol NSC vote to DNA damage in 2/4 wells at low similarities 0.50-0.61 and the single discordant 10 uM well.

What misled me was the atlas comparison: early k-neighbours 6/10 Protein synthesis (e4) shifting to 8/10 DNA damage (e9), and the 10 uM well (e3) with only 234 cells and a different profile of nuc_dna_integrated z=+16.5. The dose-response checks were also ambiguous: frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.95 (e10) and flat nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.11 (e11) and frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.11 (e12) did not show simple dose-dependent polyploidy increase.

Acquisition choices helped: the intermediate 3 uM well and 1 uM replicate proved persistence of the phenotype versus a single-well artefact. I missed an opportunity to acquire a very low dose to show onset, or to directly test Eg5/microtubule-stabilizer alternatives with spindle morphology, and the literature searches after unblinding were uninformative for linking the phenotype.

What was right:
- Prioritized replicated frac_large_nucleus z=+59 to +71.6 with nuc_form_factor z=-38 to -39 and nuc_solidity z=-31 to -53 across e2, e7, e8 as failed-cytokinesis polyploidy.
- Used microscopist Aurora candidate call with intact tubulin/actin and similar density (e5) to outweigh weak NSC vote.
- Correctly treated protocol NSC majority DNA damage 2/4 at similarities 0.50-0.61 and single-well Protein synthesis / Microtubule stabilizer calls as low-confidence.
- Used low frac_mitotic_like dose-response rho=+0.11 (e12) to argue against Eg5 mitotic-arrest alternative.

What was wrong or missed:
- Early kNN 6/10 Protein synthesis (e4) then 8/10 DNA damage (e9) was misleading and retained DNA damage at 0.23 without explaining Aurora-DNA response overlap.
- Discordant 10 uM well e3 with cell drop to 234 cells was dismissed as high-dose exception without testing toxicity / selection as cause.
- Negative frac_large_nucleus dose rho=-0.95 (e10) and flat nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.11 (e11) contradicted simple polyploidy expectation and were under-interpreted; a low-dose onset well instead of a second 1 uM replicate might have clarified.

Proposed next experiment: DNA-content flow cytometry for ploidy plus phospho-histone H3 Ser10 immunofluorescence across 0.01-10 uM AZ841 versus DMSO and a reference Aurora inhibitor, with tubulin staining to confirm failed cytokinesis / multinucleation and exclude monopolar Eg5 spindles.
